'''Ōminakuchi no Sukune''' (大水口宿禰) is a figure in ancient {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}, identified as an early ancestor of the {{ill|Hozumi clan|ja|穂積氏|qid=Q11597079}}. His name does not appear in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}.''

== Lineage ==
The ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'' and ''Kojiki'' do not provide explicit details about his lineage. However, the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'' attributes his ancestry to {{ill|Ikaga Shikoo|ja|伊香賀色雄}} and Shinkawa Kodatehime, or alternatively, as a sixth-generation descendant of {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}.

In contrast, the ''{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}'' refers to him as a son of Izushi Kokoro no Ōmi no Mikoto and Shinkawa Kodatehime, with some discrepancies between sources.<ref name="keifu4" /> 

No historical texts explicitly identify his children.

== Historical Records ==
According to the ''Nihon Shoki,'' on the 7th day of the 8th month of the 7th year of Emperor Sujin's reign, Ōminakuchi no Sukune, along with {{ill|Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime|ja|倭迹速神浅茅原目妙姫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatototohimomoso no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 倭迹迹日百襲姫命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11387098}} and {{ill|Ise no Omi no Kimi|ja|伊勢麻績君}}, had the same divine revelation in a dream. They relayed to the emperor that {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}} and {{ill|Yamato Okunitama|en|Yamato Okunitama|qid=Q11387080|lt=Yamato no Ōkunitama}} should be enshrined by {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子}} and {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichiiso Nagaoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q18700600}} respectively.<ref name="tenson" />

In the 25th year of Emperor Suinin's reign, an alternate account states that the deity of Yamato took possession of Ōminakuchi no Sukune, directing him to perform its worship.

== Descendants ==
=== Clans ===
The ''Nihon Shoki'' names Ōminakuchi no Sukune as a distant ancestor of the {{ill|Hozumi clan|ja|穂積氏|qid=Q11597079}}.

The ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'' also identifies the following clans as his descendants:
* '''Sakyō Shinbetsu Tenjin Hozumi Clan''' - Descendants of Ōminakuchi no Sukune, son of Ikaga Shikoo.
* '''Ukyō Shinbetsu Tenjin Uneme Clan''' - Descendants of Ōminakuchi no Sukune, sixth-generation descendant of Nigihayahi.

The ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'' similarly identifies Ōminakuchi no Sukune as an ancestor of the Hozumi and Uneme clans.<ref name="keifu4" />

=== Provincial Governors ===
The ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'' describes descendants of Ōminakuchi no Sukune serving as provincial governors:
* '''Matsura no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' - During Emperor Seimu's reign, {{ill|Yada Ineyoshi no Mikoto|ja|矢田稲吉命}}, a grandson of Ōminakuchi Ashinai, was appointed governor of the Matsura region (modern-day {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|qid=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}} and {{ill|Matsura-gun|en|Matsura-gun|qid=Q5973791|lt=Matsuura District, Nagasaki}}).<ref>''Research on the Kokuzō System - Historical Materials and Analysis'' (Yagi Shoten, 2013), p. 280.</ref>
